trajectory_summary: The call opens neutral and builds real engagement once the rep asks about the customer's interest — Zachary volunteers a genuine two-year regret narrative and a concrete bill figure. From there the call flattens into a long, patient but repetitive bill-collection slog that never pivots channels, and it closes on a tentative, contingent appointment rather than a locked booking. The rep held the send-proposal-before-meeting hard rule cleanly but left the customer's own compelling data points (regret framing, near-doubled usage) largely unflipped into urgency.
outcome_dispute: The call ends with 'let's tentatively plan for that, and I'll let you know if that doesn't work' plus an explicit rep-side fallback plan ('if I don't hear back from you, we'll call Monday morning just to make sure that time still works'). This is a conditional/tentative booking, not a firm booked appointment — the customer never confirms without a contingency, and the rep's own language treats Monday 3:30 as unconfirmed pending the customer's work schedule.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: button-up mechanics on a fragile booking
primary_coaching_focus.quote: We'll tentatively schedule you for Monday at 03:30. And, again, you've got my info, so if things change, just let me know.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The appointment is explicitly conditional in the customer's own words, and the rep's close skips the hour-block statement, the no-driving/computer instruction, and the 'is that fair?' handshake — the exact elements the schema flags as predictive of show rate. On an already-hedging customer, these are the highest-leverage lines to firm things up, and the rep left all of them out.
